notes: Figure 2 maps named ratio variants to TEM panels; same physical batch for XRD and TEM is not established.

intuition.title: Prepared polymer is the template reagent
intuition.text: The record starts from 10 mg of a prepared star-brush copolymer in 10 mL DMF. Its upstream synthesis partly follows prior work and is not reconstructed as a complete independent route here.

intuition.title: Figure 2 has source-label disagreements
intuition.text: Panel i caption says DLS/TEM while the plot legend says DLS/AFM; the Figure 2 caption also mislabels the rightmost j plot as h. No numerical route value is taken from the disputed plot.

intuition.title: XPS belongs to Template-4
intuition.text: Figure 3c/d XPS is Template-4 context only. Figure 3a/b compares all four named routes, while the Ag fcc viewer is an external reference rather than measured coordinates.

scopeLabel: Ag@Template-3, AgNO3:AA ratio 2:5 in p.3 synthesis; main PDF pp.1–6 of 13 and Figures 2–3 independently scoped. SI and biological assays were not reviewed. Template-3 ratio conflict remains unresolved.

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
